result.title: Adversarial Attacks Expose Path-Dependent Failures in Discrete Medical Image Tokenizers
result.comment: 21 pages, 9 figures, 18 tables. Accepted at the GenAI4Health Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026, Sydney
result.summary: Discrete image tokenizers convert medical images into token sequences that downstream models either decode into an image for a classifier (the reconstruction path), classify directly (the token path), or feed to a generative multimodal model. We ask whether imperceptible input perturbations can break these systems through the tokenizer alone. We evaluate four tokenizers on three imaging modalities and extend the strongest attack to a deployed generative model. Our central finding is path-dependence: the same tokenizer fails in opposite ways depending on how its output is used. A supervised attack collapses diagnostic accuracy on the reconstruction path, with ROC AUC falling to $\leq 0.013$ at $ε=2/255$ on all four tokenizers, while sparing the token path. An unsupervised, label-free attack does the reverse; its damage concentrates in the multi-codebook tokenizers, worst in MedITok, whose token-path AUC falls from 0.919 to 0.239. The same label-free attack transfers to LLaVA-Med, a frozen medical vision-language model built on MedITok, making it report proliferative diabetic retinopathy in a healthy retina or call a malignant lesion benign, without access to the question, answer, or language-model gradients. Harm is driven by how far the attack moves the tokenizer's internal representation, not by how many tokens change: on the learned-codebook tokenizers, a control attack that changes nearly all tokens but moves the representation less leaves every path and answer intact. Domain-specific pretraining does not provide robustness: MedITok has the best clean accuracy yet is the most fragile, more so than UniTok, its general-domain counterpart. None of six candidate defenses repairs every failure mode, and several fail once the attacker optimizes against the defense directly. Medical tokenizer robustness must therefore be evaluated per downstream path, against an adaptive adversary.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在三种医学影像模态上对四个离散图像 tokenizer 做对抗攻击，发现失败模式存在「路径依赖」：有监督攻击重创重建路径而放过 token 路径，无标签攻击则相反并集中于多码本 tokenizer，且可无梯度迁移到基于 MedITok 的 LLaVA-Med 造成错误诊断。
AI.relevance_reason: 与「视觉细节是否保留在内部状态」「答案是否真正使用 latent 视觉内容」直接相关：其核心结论是伤害取决于 tokenizer 内部表示移动幅度而非改动 token 数，可用于核查视觉旁路与信息坍缩，重建路径与 token/生成路径的分裂也提示需按下游用法分别评估 latent 状态质量。
